content.title: About
content.content: Granulated sugar is the crystalline form of sugar derived from sugarcane or beet. It consists of fine, uniform crystals that dissolve easily in liquids and is widely used in cooking, baking, and beverages.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Granulated sugar typically contains 99.9 % pure sucrose.
The crystals form during the crystallization process when a saturated solution is cooled.
In the United States it is often called “white sugar,” while in Russia it is known as “песочный сахар.”
Sugar is used not only in food production but also in pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and as a preservative.
Crystal size can vary from fine (for drinks) to coarse (for topping baked goods).

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: Sugar is rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate supply of glucose to cells.

items.title: Flavor enhancement
items.content: Sugar amplifies taste perception, making foods more palatable.

items.title: Texture preservation
items.content: In baking, sugar helps create a crisp crust and retains moisture, improving product structure.

items.title: Increased risk of cavities
items.content: Frequent sugar consumption promotes dental caries.

items.title: Impact on blood sugar levels
items.content: Excessive sugar can cause rapid glucose spikes, which is critical for people with diabetes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Sugar provides 4 kcal per gram, so overconsumption may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: A small number of individuals may be sensitive to processing additives used in sugar.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Granulated sugar is used to sweeten beverages, baked goods, sauces, marinades, and desserts. It can be sprinkled on fruit, added to dough, or dissolved in hot liquids.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sugar in an airtight container in a dry, cool place away from moisture and direct sunlight. If moisture gets in, crystals may clump, and prolonged exposure to heat can cause darkening.
